sections.h2: Where is Bend, Oregon, and what is the terrain like?
sections.html:
Bend is a Central Oregon city on the Deschutes River, east of the Cascade Range, and it is the county seat of Deschutes County. It covers about 35 square miles at an elevation near 3,640 feet.

Pilot Butte, an extinct cinder cone, stands inside city limits. The Horse Lava Tube System borders the east side, Newberry National Volcanic Monument lies just south, and Deschutes National Forest touches the southwest edge. Across Deschutes County the U.S. Forest Service owns about 51 percent of the land.

Bend's 2020 census population was 99,178, up 29.4 percent from 76,639 in 2010. The Wikipedia summary of Census Bureau data gives an estimate of 106,926 for 2024.

Bend takes its name from a bend in the Deschutes River that pioneers forded, and it was platted in 1904 and incorporated in January 1905. A dam built in 1910 created Mirror Pond, and Deschutes County was formed in 1916 with Bend as its seat.

Lumber carried the early economy. When the Shevlin-Hixon Lumber mill closed in 1950, the region took its largest economic drop since the Great Depression. POWDR Corp. bought Mt. Bachelor in 2001.

sections.h2: What are the biggest employers in Bend?
sections.html:
St. Charles Health System is Bend's largest employer, followed by the Bend-La Pine School District. Tourism is also a major sector: Travel Oregon reported in 2019 that the local industry employed about 10,000 people.

Employer (2023)Employees
St. Charles Health System3,506
Bend-La Pine School District2,300
Deschutes County1,284
Mount Bachelor1,081
City of Bend717

Retirement and commuting to tech jobs in the Bay Area and Seattle also drive growth. Visitors matter to the local budget: transient room tax revenue topped $7.8 million from July 2024 to March 2025. Deschutes Brewery is the largest of more than 30 breweries in the city, and four destination resorts, including Sunriver, are major employers in the wider county. That visitor economy is why the short-term rental rules below come up so often.

sections.h2: What is Bend's climate and how does it affect a house?
sections.html:
Bend has a cold semi-arid climate with light precipitation but real winters. The city gets about 10.6 inches of precipitation and 21.6 inches of snow a year. January highs average 42.5 degrees and lows 24.6. July highs average 83.8.

The record low is minus 26, and freezing temperatures are possible from about mid-September to mid-June. Summer days can swing 35 degrees from high to low.

  • Frozen pipes and shallow water lines are a winter risk in vacant houses
  • Roof snow load and ice dams matter for older roofs
  • Dry summers raise wildfire concerns for houses near trees and the national forest
  • Big day and night swings stress paint, decks and exterior wood

A house left empty over winter can develop plumbing damage quickly, and an inherited or second-home property is often vacant.

sections.h2: How does wildfire risk affect selling a Bend house?
sections.html:
Wildfire risk shows up in Bend as insurance cost and availability, not as a statewide map. Oregon's legislature passed Senate Bill 83 in 2025 to repeal the state wildfire hazard map and its building code requirements.

Before the repeal, Deschutes County had 21,258 lots classified as high hazard. A 2023 law already barred insurers from using the map for pricing or coverage. Central Oregon owners still reported large premium increases and coverage cutbacks, and the state notes that insurers use their own models.

The Oregon Division of Financial Regulation lists these defensible space steps:

  • Clear dry leaves, brush and pine needles from the yard and gutters
  • Trim trees back from the structure
  • Screen open vents

If your Bend house has fire-prone landscaping or a rough roof, an as-is sale lets the buyer decide how to handle it. The state's page on wildfire and insurance explains policyholder rights.

sections.h2: Which parts of Bend are there, and what are the schools?
sections.html:
Bend has 13 official neighborhood districts: Awbrey Butte, Boyd Acres, Century West, Larkspur, Mountain View, Old Bend, Old Farm District, Orchard District, River West, Southeast Bend, Southern Crossing, Southwest Bend and Summit West.

The Bend-La Pine School District has six high schools, six middle schools and 19 elementary schools, three of them magnet schools. Central Oregon Community College and OSU-Cascades are also in Bend.

Housing tenure in 2020 was 60.6 percent owner-occupied and 39.4 percent renter-occupied, with 44,449 housing units.

sections.h2: How do roads, buses and airports connect Bend?
sections.html:
US 20 and US 97 meet in Bend, and US 97 runs through the city as the Bend Parkway. Century Drive, Highway 372, leads to Mt. Bachelor.

Roberts Field in Redmond, 18 miles north, has direct flights to cities including Seattle, Denver, Los Angeles and San Francisco. Bend Municipal Airport handles general aviation. The nearest Amtrak station is in Chemult, about 65 miles south. Cascades East Transit runs nine fixed bus routes from the Hawthorne Transit Center.

sections.h2: What are the short-term rental rules if my Bend house is a vacation rental?
sections.html:
Bend requires a land use permit and an operating license for most short-term rentals, and permits approved after April 15, 2015 end when the property sells. A short-term rental is a stay of fewer than 30 consecutive days.

  • Operating licenses are never transferable
  • Permits approved on or before April 15, 2015 run with the land, and the new owner must apply for an operating license within 60 days of closing
  • A City of Bend business registration is required
  • Most rentals owe a 10.4 percent room tax on gross revenue

In practice, a buyer of a vacation rental cannot assume the rental income will carry over. Check with the City's Licensing office, at 541-388-5580 extension 8, and planning at extension 3 before you promote the house as an income property. The city's short-term rental page lists current fees, which the sources I read showed in conflicting amounts.

sections.h2: Can I sell a Bend rental with a tenant in place?
sections.html:
Yes, and with 39.4 percent of Bend housing renter-occupied in 2020, many owners do. Oregon's ORS 90.427 limits ending a tenancy for a sale: after the tenant's first year, a landlord needs an accepted offer from a buyer who will live in the home and must give at least 90 days of written notice.

The landlord also owes one month's rent when delivering that notice, unless the landlord owns four or fewer covered units. A landlord who breaks the rule can owe three months' rent plus damages, so a sale that keeps the lease in place is often the lower-risk route.

sections.h2: How do Deschutes County property taxes work for a Bend seller?
sections.html:
Deschutes County sends Bend property tax statements in October, and the first installment and the full-pay discount fall in mid-November. For the 2025 bills, the deadline was November 17, with a 3 percent discount for paying in full and 2 percent for paying two thirds.

Installment (2025 bills)Date
Full pay or first thirdNovember 17
Second thirdFebruary 17
Final installmentMay 15

Central Oregon Daily reported that Deschutes County property taxes were expected to rise about 4 percent in 2025, depending on location. The county's tax office is at 541-388-6540 or taxoffice@deschutes.org, and the county asks owners to update a mailing address before September 30 so the statement reaches the right place.

If you sell mid-year, the escrow company prorates the bill between you and the buyer. Oregon's Department of Revenue lists December 31 as the appeal deadline to the county Board of Property Tax Appeals.

faqs.a: Yes. Bend is the county seat of Deschutes County, which was formed on December 13, 1916.

faqs.q: Does selling a Bend vacation rental transfer the short-term rental permit?
faqs.a: Not for newer permits. Permits approved after April 15, 2015 are tied to the owner and become void when the property sells, and operating licenses never transfer.

faqs.q: What is Bend's coldest recorded temperature?
faqs.a: The record low is minus 26 degrees, recorded in January and February, according to the Wikipedia climate summary.

faqs.q: When are Bend property taxes due?
faqs.a: For the 2025 bills, the full-pay deadline was November 17, with the later installments due February 17 and May 15. Dates move when November 15 lands on a weekend.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Bend house with wildfire risk or old landscaping?
faqs.a: Yes. Oregon repealed its state wildfire hazard map in 2025, but insurers still price risk with their own models, so buyers should expect questions about defensible space.
